extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Army commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), social media managers, and other Army personnel responsible for public engagement and communications
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs activities including air demonstrations, public engagement programs, speaker/manuscript clearance, writing style, and digital/social media management. Covers responsibilities, approval/clearance procedures, content standards, and operational constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft performance demonstration eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Aircraft performance record demonstrations are restricted to aircraft assigned to an operational unit of a military service for at least 6 months. Demonstrations that imply competition between military services are not authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety and operational procedures are in AR 95-1. If only Army aircraft participate designate a nonparticipating Army aviator as controller; when multiple services participate a senior military controller will be designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flight demonstration controller responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller is responsible for coordinating between the event sponsor and the Armed Forces participants; ensuring that flight and safety regulations of the military departments and FAA are observed; and ensuring flying time devoted to aircraft participation is used to the fullest extent for combat readiness or training purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller designation rules depend on participating services; see AR 95-1 for safety and operational procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assault and helicopter troop landing demonstrations restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Assault aircraft demonstrations and helicopter troop landings under simulated tactical conditions, when conducted for public viewing, are restricted to military installations capable of supporting such activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities should not be held at public venues that cannot support the necessary safety and operational requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAA waiver requirement for public aerial demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The event sponsor is required to obtain an FAA waiver for any public demonstration by military aircraft or parachutists. An FAA waiver is normally required at least 60 days prior to the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final authorization depends on the event sponsor securing a waiver far enough in advance to permit adequate planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support contingent on resource availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for aerial demonstrations depends on the availability of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for demonstrations should consider resource constraints and command priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize recruiting benefit at public events
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum advantage for Army recruiting will be taken at public events where aerial demonstrations are authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination should be made with the appropriate Army recruiting battalion and PA office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official public engagement program examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Command-initiated programs effective in informing the public include an active speaker’s bureau program; ongoing liaison with external organizations; participatory membership in civic, business, and professional organizations; exhibits, bands, color guards, and other ceremonial units; periodic open houses; installation tour programs; participating in national holiday observances; supporting overseas host nation activities; supporting local veterans and military service organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders should use these official programs to develop and maintain a viable relationship with the civilian community within resource and operational limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for unofficial public engagement programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should encourage military and civilian personnel and their Family members to participate as private persons in local community activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military personnel lending voluntary support during off-duty time may be authorized to participate in uniform if consistent with DoD 5500.07-R; see AR 670-1 for appropriate off-duty uniform wear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community liaison responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders must maintain continual liaison with persons and organizations in the local community to help resolve common problems and develop cooperation and understanding between the installation and the local community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison actions include: developing effective two-way communication, fostering cooperation among civilian and military agencies, providing maximum support of Army activities, supporting recruiting, participating in/hosting civic/professional/business clubs, promoting USMA and ROTC scholarship opportunities, promoting use of ARNG armories or USAR centers by civic organizations, and ensuring any civilian advisory committees comply with AR 15-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal community engagement working group duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders are encouraged to organize informal community engagement working groups composed of military and civilian staff members and subordinate commanders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum these forums should plan a continuous community engagement program; establish and maintain contact with civilian service, business, economic, professional, minority, veterans and military service organizations; maintain contact with key civilian officials; evaluate effects of command operations and advise commander of actions to reduce adverse reaction; maintain a consistent orientation program on community engagement; promote new ways for command members to participate in local activities; and conduct periodic appraisals of public attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community surveys and privacy constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Community surveys and analyses are helpful in developing a sound public engagement program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys must not violate FOIA or Privacy Act regulations or AR 380-13 concerning acquisition and storage of information on nonaffiliated persons and organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising support limitations and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Army support may be provided to United/federated/joint fundraising campaigns authorized by AR 600-29; appeals authorized by the President or OPM; and efforts sponsored by military service aid societies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD 5500.07-R governs Army support for local fundraising events. Volunteer off-duty efforts by Army personnel as private individuals are permissible. Fundraising concerts by military bands limited to specified sponsors; exceptions possible if benefits are widespread. COCOM commanders may authorize exceptions overseas (except HI and AK) to permit participation in athletic competitions to support local fundraising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with state and local officials requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Within national security and congressional constraints, state and local officials must be consulted at the earliest stages of planning major policy, budget, or reorganization proposals that have significant state and local impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands should contact OCPA when they know of or receive an inquiry about a local or congressional issue; OCPA will provide consultation guidance based on DoD guidance. No early consultation without HQDA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant days and observances policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Army birthday (June 14), Army Reserve birthday (April 23), Armed Forces Day (third Saturday of May) and Veterans Day (Nov 11) are recognized observances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD policy provides military support for AFD and Veterans Day observances at DoD-designated regional sites and, as resources permit, for smaller local observances. AFD commemorative editions of unit/newspapers may be published with messages from commanders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house purpose and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: An open house is a military program conducted on an installation or other military facility to which the general public is invited to present military missions, equipment, facilities, and personnel to a civilian community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders encouraged to hold at least one open house annually within resource limits; ensure proper security review; displays should come primarily from host installation or local community; may invite assets from other installations; encourage participation by Family Readiness Groups and general public; use ARNG armories, USAR and Air Force Reserve centers as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to state governor's inaugural activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint military service support to state governor's inaugural ceremonies and parades is appropriate subject to availability of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for additional assets go through the chain of command; report circumstances to ATSD(PA) if no troops/resources in state; bands/units/equipment from outside local area may be provided only if no additional cost unless approved by ATSD(PA); support should be limited in size and scope; ARNG may be ordered to state duty; duties conform to DoDI 5410.19; approved ARNG flyovers authorized only when flown in conjunction with a scheduled training mission at no additional expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: JCOC nominee eligibility and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint Civilian Orientation Conference (JCOC) is sponsored by the Secretary of Defense for in-depth orientation to military missions. Nominees must be influential leaders in their professions and communities and cannot possess extensive DoD knowledge or strong existing relationships with senior military.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only U.S. citizens not eligible are prior participants, partisan public officials, political candidates, persons engaged in paid partisan activities, those drawing any federal paycheck, or salaried employees of government contractors whose primary duties are military related. Participants are expected to share experiences with colleagues after the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Army support to non-government authors/producers
rubrics_metrics.description: Army installations/commands may assist authors and producers; support forwarded to OCPA when subject is of regional/national interest or distributed outside local area. Support provided only when cooperation benefits DA/DoD or is in the national interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product must be authentic in portrayal of persons/places/operations/historical events or, if fictional, depict military life plausibly; must foster improved understanding of the Army; cannot condone or endorse activities contrary to U.S. Government policy or Army/DoD interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for entertainment industry support
rubrics_metrics.description: OCPA-West processes requests for film, television, and multimedia entertainment-oriented projects; PAOs should request the OCPA-West guide when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appearances by Army personnel in an official capacity or in uniform must be approved based on level of interest; participation must be unique in character, not have a commercial counterpart, and be in DA/DoD interest; sponsor must agree before broadcast to satisfy all copyright requirements; talk show appearances with regional/national interest require OCPA coordination; promotional assistance and branding issues submitted to OCPA; Army themes/materiel/uniforms/insignia cannot be used in ads/promotions implying endorsement unless part of an approved Army marketing initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster relief and civil disturbance PA coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs will coordinate with FEMA, DHS, Northern Command, U.S. Army North, and OCPA during disaster relief operations. OCPA is responsible for PA activities in connection with civil disturbances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon conclusion of disaster relief, PAOs must provide OCPA a narrative summary of PA activities and their results and provide information copies to intermediate headquarters. Refer civil disturbance public information matters to OCPA; ARNG units on non-federal status should coordinate with NGB-PA. Coordinate crisis communications with U.S. Army North and OCPA and transmit VI content via the Defense Visual Information Distribution Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory clearance for official speeches and writings
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearance through security review and PA channels is required for all official speeches and writings presented or published in the civilian domain, including materials placed on the internet or released via similar digital media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual speechwriters, authors, and speakers are responsible for ensuring content review and clearance prior to public release. See DoDI 5230.09 for additional info on releasing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearance authorities and prepublication review
rubrics_metrics.description: HQDA or OSD clearance is required for speeches, manuscripts, or communications meeting criteria in paragraph 7-6. Information proposed for posting on public internet sites must be reviewed and approved by the appropriate proponent office prior to release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material mentioning names of military personnel, DoD employees, military operations, or subjects listed in 7-6a(1)-(20) must be submitted for prepublication review prior to release to non-DoD persons, including ghostwriters, agents, editors, or publishers. Unofficial materials not dealing with the military do not require clearance; however, authors are responsible to ensure security has not been compromised. Open source material does not equal declassification and combining open sources may create classified content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speakers at nonfederal entities compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel serving as speakers or panel members at conferences must comply with AR 1-50 and DoD 5500.07-R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers must safeguard procurement, technology, classified, and nonpublic information and must not appear to endorse nonfederal entities. Approval authorities should consult legal advisors before authorizing participation at nonfederal entity conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal of Honor recipient appearance protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Special attention is required for public appearances by Medal of Honor (MOH) recipients to balance recognition with protection from exploitation and overexposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the recipient's personal preferences and event value equally; discourage appearances at schools to protect their training/education; obtain proper clearances for absences from duty; sponsors pay transportation/food/lodging if required; local commanders may approve appearances outside local area; supporting PAO forwards biography and photograph to OCPA and maintains/updates it as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official speaking/writing content constraints and review purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Speeches or remarks must address subjects within a speaker's official expertise. Official speeches and writings must not contradict U.S. Government policy or law and must adhere to DoD 5500.07-R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and clearance at the lowest competent level is required for security, accuracy, policy, and propriety and is not censorship but a safeguard. Full text is preferred for review; outlines/slides may be reviewed to keep PAOs informed. Generally, Army employees will not officially endorse membership drives or fundraisers for nonfederal entities. Avoid events whose real purpose is controversy; consult OCPA before providing speakers for planned public confrontation or debate of national policy. Material must not promote private individuals or give appearance of endorsement; participation only if accommodations available without discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media interview and distribution guidance for speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Press, radio, and television interviews in conjunction with speaking engagements are encouraged, subject to regulation and Army PA policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army speakers should consult their Army PA office before media interviews. Advance distribution of cleared material is encouraged to gain widest dissemination and speech texts may be distributed in cooperation with the host organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revalidation and appeals for clearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to repetitively using a previously cleared speech or manuscript, the clearance should be revalidated by the approving PAO. Denials or directed mandatory changes may be appealed through original submission channels to OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials that require HQDA or OSD clearance must be submitted with full and final text (including VI) sufficiently in advance for review. Manuscripts lacking proper clearance submitted to official Army publications will be sent by editors to the proper clearance authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial and academic publication exceptions and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals may write articles for official DoD publications if manuscripts are cleared prior to publication. Students and faculty at DoD academic institutions are not required to submit papers prepared for academic requirements when not intended for release outside the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials intended for public release or made available in public-access libraries must be submitted for review and clearance if classified info is not disclosed and DoD interests not jeopardized. Unofficial writings using DoD identification must include a disclaimer stating views are author's and do not reflect official policy. Acceptance of payment for unofficial speeches/writings must comply with relevant ethics regulations. Notes/abstracts will not substitute for complete text (but abstracts published in advance require clearance). Retired personnel should use DoD security review to ensure no compromise of national security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local speaking and manuscript clearance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: PAO will establish local clearance procedures; most clearances will be completed at the local level and there is no requirement to submit material for clearance to HQDA based solely on author rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If HQDA/OSD clearance required, submit full/final texts including VI, allow sufficient time, and appeal denials through original channels. Material originating in Army components of unified/joint commands will be cleared according to those command procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing style references
rubrics_metrics.description: The Associated Press (AP) Stylebook and DoD Visual Information Style Guide are the primary references for writing effective captions and stories. The Army.mil Style Guide supplements the AP Stylebook for DoD-specific issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Army.mil Style Guide for military-specific terms describing Servicemembers, equipment, places, and entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital media definition and PA responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital media is defined as text, audio, and visual information (VI) content that can be transmitted over the internet or computer networks. Using digital media to communicate on behalf of the Army is a PA function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army PA content released on websites, blogs, or social media platforms falls into this category and must follow this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media purpose and professionalism requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A social media presence must have a well-defined purpose, clearly align with the command’s communication objectives, and remain a credible source of information for the public. Army social media platforms are official representations of the U.S. Army and must demonstrate professionalism at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial social media sites are not owned by the Army; commanders must ensure platforms reflect command objectives and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCPA Digital Media Division functions
rubrics_metrics.description: OCPA Digital Media Division serves as the Army's main representative and liaison for commercial social media platforms, manages HQDA level social media platforms, develops guidance, maintains the Army Social Media Guide, develops social media guidance, maintains approved social media training lists, approves official social media sites for registration, and maintains a working group with major command social media managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Army Social Media Guide (https://www.army.mil/socialmedia) explains standard operating procedures for official external presences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanders' social media responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders will provide authorization to establish official social media accounts in compliance with local network restrictions; authorize social media managers to release information on the command’s behalf; ensure social media managers are trained and certified; ensure managers have proper equipment and network access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brigade level and above are encouraged to use social media as part of communication strategy; lower echelon units should coordinate with higher echelon PA offices if separate presence not warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAOs' social media oversight duties
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs for ACOMs, ASCCs, DRUs, or designated representatives will ensure approved social media sites operate within guidelines, provide accurate information, register platforms in the Army social media directory, and maintain a roster/network of social media managers within the command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should ensure compliance with regulation and accuracy of public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media manager responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media managers must manage accounts using only authorized Government equipment; ensure sites operate within guidelines; update content regularly and consistently; publish properly reviewed, released, and public domain information and imagery; actively engage the public through timely and accurate information while maintaining security and privacy; archive and close inactive or noncompliant accounts; develop and update local SOPs; treat social media access/passwords with as much care as PII; maintain a continuity book/file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity book should include a roster of authorized accounts and admins; social media processes and strategy including a public defacement response plan and justification of platform needs; appointment letters for each approved unit's social media manager. Appointment letters and sites should be reviewed annually; review content for OPSEC before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel who manage and release information on official Army social media platforms must be OPSEC level II certified and current with required social media training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Army Social Media Guide and OCPA maintain lists of approved training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media registration criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The social media directory registers official social media accounts of organizations with a 1035 civilian or 46 series military occupational specialty with release authority that is OPSEC level II trained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pages must be open to the public; private groups, accounts, or feeds will not be registered in the Army social media directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release authority for social media managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media managers on official Army social media accounts must be granted release authority by the commanding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release authority must be renewed during command and personnel changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media disclaimers and account settings requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Army social media platforms must be labeled as an official account, classified as a Government organization, and include specific user terms of agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User terms must include a general disclaimer, privacy and security disclaimers, copyright and trademark disclaimers, moderated account disclaimer, FOIA notice, negotiated terms wording from GSA, contact information (valid .mil or .gov email), and an official URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media content priorities and prohibited topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations will have a list of communication priorities as a basis for items that should be posted and a working list of topics that should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lists are determined by the commander's priorities and the public's needs and should be used to guide posting decisions.
